agent_notes: The text gives no date for Dinah's outing. I anchored it on the altar at Shechem (33:20) with an offset of 5 years and a margin of 3 years (so 2 to 8 years after it), at MACRO_ERA because the gap is an estimate. Revised at the reviewer's request (first from 6 months to 3 years ± 2, now later): the age arithmetic was redone on the linked dates. Dinah is about Joseph's age (both about 8 at the altar) and Simeon and Levi 4-5 years older; the earlier window gave Dinah only about 9-13, so I moved it later, keeping the upper end (about 1900 BCE) before Joseph's 17th year (37:2, about 1899 BCE). The window stays inside the period before ch. 35 (Jacob leaves Shechem at Bethel's command) and Joseph's 17th year (37:2). The packet offers no commentary on the length of the stay.

agent_notes: Jacob's hearing is placed right after the assault (no stated delay), with a margin of a day. The sons are in the field with the livestock (34:5), so the interval until they return is open; I kept it short because Hamor sets out at once and the sons arrive while he is speaking (34:6–7).

history.note: [consider] Make the duration run until the sons' arrival, or say in the note that the two are meant to meet. (GEN.34.5: 'Jacob held his peace until they were come')

agent_notes: 'On the third day' is counted from the circumcision day as day 1 (Radak, Ibn Ezra: the third day is when the wound is most painful), so offset 2 days from the start of the circumcision. If the circumcision took place over a day, the margin of 12 hours covers it. Hebrew day (sunset to sunset) versus civil day is not resolved by the text.

history.note: [consider] Use a neutral phrase such as 'come upon the city, which was off its guard' only if you mean Onkelos's reading, or else 'come boldly upon the city'. Either is fine; a short note on the ambiguity is enough. (GEN.34.25: 'came upon the city boldly' (KJV); YLT 'come in against the city confidently'; Onkelos 'the city that dwelt in security')

agent_notes: The sons come 'when they heard', so the event begins shortly after Hamor leaves; the text does not say whether they arrived before or during Hamor's speech. I placed it before the proposal (8) as the sons are addressed in 34:8 ('with them').

notes.note: All 31 verses are covered. Verses 18–19 are one event (the brothers' terms please Hamor and Shechem), verses 27–29 one event (the plunder). Verse 31 (the brothers' reply) is folded into Jacob's rebuke.

No divine or prophetic speech in this chapter, so there are no FULFILLS_PROPHECY links. Jacob's fear of attack in 34:30 is not fulfilled in this chapter; ch. 35:5 (terror of God on the cities) is the likely counterpoint, and that chapter's session may link it. The chapter also is the cause of Jacob's later words about Simeon and Levi (Gen 49:5–7).
